main_text.p: la[?],quæ omnium cruditatū parens est:quandoquidem ad arthritidis generatione non sola quæritur articulorum imbecillitas,sed &quæ in illos defluant excrementa. Qua-propter podagram Bacchi & Veneris pro-lem esse finxerunt Græci poetæ. Cæterum utra causarum nimirum venus, vel crapula ad arthritidis ortum sit[?] potior, nunc nobis videndum. Idcirco proponuntur capi, qui tamersi[?] castrati sint,nihilominus tamen po-dagra miris afficiuntur modis. At vero gallinacei omnino veneri dediti, multo-que humore prædicti (alioqui ne unus qui-de tot gallinis sufficeret) podagra nequaquam laborant. Adde quod in his multus calor adest, & cibi non magna abstinentia: in illis vero pusillus calor ob testium refe-ctionem, & multa edacitas, ex qua nō par-væ gignuntur cruditates. Propterea ad ar-thritidis procreationem plus crapulam fa-cere, quam venerem quispiam collegerit. His adde quod illa utranq; præbet articu-laris morbi causam, hæc vero duntaxat effi-cientem. At vero longe aliter se res haber[?]. Nam immoderata venus ac intempestiva non solùm articulos laxat, & ex accidenti refrigerat: sed etiam vinculis, quibus com-mittun-

page.notes: The first letter of the page's opening word is uncertain: it could be I or L, so "la[?]" is marked. "sit" and "tamersi" are doubtful readings (the scan shows "fit" and "tamerfi"; long s is written as plain s). "haber" may be a printing error for "habet"; it is kept as printed and marked. The bottom signature "R 2" and catchword "mittun-" are on the same line. The page is a continuation with no indented paragraph breaks, so it is one paragraph.
